questions.question: What risks does NVIDIA's FY2026 10-K associate with its acquisitions and strategic investments, including its planned OpenAI deal?

answer.text:
NVIDIA says acquisitions and investments involve significant challenges and risks and could impair its ability to grow its business, develop new products or sell its products, and ultimately hurt its financial results [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Pursuing one transaction may limit its ability to enter other transactions [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Technology could also evolve and make an acquisition less attractive [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Regulators could impose conditions that reduce an acquisition's ultimate value, and harm to its perceived ability to complete acquisitions could make future ones more difficult, complex or expensive [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
On investments, NVIDIA says they could create volatility and fluctuations in its results, with realized and unrealized gains or losses, and it could lose up to the full value of an investment [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Many investee companies may not achieve profitability in the near term, or at all, and there is no guarantee of a return [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Investments in private companies include early-stage companies still defining their strategic direction, and many of the securities are non-marketable and illiquid at the time of initial investment [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. If investees are unsuccessful, NVIDIA could recognize an impairment or lose all or part of its investment [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Its investment portfolio also has industry sector concentration risks, and a decline in one or more sectors could increase impairment losses [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
They also include difficulty obtaining governmental or regulatory approvals, consents or financing, legal proceedings arising from a deal, and the potential failure of due diligence to identify significant issues [0001045810-26-000021:0034]. Acquisition-specific risks include difficulty integrating technology, systems, products, operations and employees (including key personnel), assumption of liabilities, amortization expenses, goodwill impairment charges or write-downs of acquired assets, and difficulty integrating accounting, forecasting and controls [0001045810-26-000021:0034].
On OpenAI, NVIDIA says it is finalizing an investment and partnership agreement, but there is no assurance that it will enter into such an agreement or that a transaction will be completed [0001045810-26-000021:0034][0001045810-26-000021:0071].
Many of these investments are illiquid and non-marketable [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. It also says its investments in publicly-held equity securities may fluctuate significantly with stock prices and could adversely affect its financial results [0001045810-26-000021:0062]. If the escrow and the partners' operating activities are not sufficient to cover an event of default, it may elect to assume the underlying leases for internal use or sublease them to third parties [0001045810-26-000021:0062].

questions.question: What charges did NVIDIA and AMD each record from the April 2025 U.S. export license requirements on their China-bound data center GPUs, and how did those charges show up in their quarterly results?

answer.text:
NVIDIA recorded a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, tied to H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations, after the U.S. government said on April 9, 2025 that exporting H20 chips to China and D:5 countries required a license [0001045810-25-000116:0028]. NVIDIA said the charge was less than it first expected because it could re-use certain materials [0001045810-25-000116:0028]. H20 sales were $4.6 billion in that quarter, before the new licensing requirements took effect [0001045810-25-000116:0028].
In NVIDIA's results, gross margin decreased from a year earlier and from the prior quarter, primarily because of the $4.5 billion charge and the initial ramp of more sophisticated systems within Data Center [0001045810-25-000116:0031]. The summary table shows gross margin of 60.5%, against 73.0% in the prior quarter and 78.4% a year earlier [0001045810-25-000116:0030]. In the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, NVIDIA recognized about $650 million of H20 revenue from sales to an unrestricted customer outside China, which resulted in a $180 million release of previously reserved H20 inventory [0001045810-25-000209:0034].
AMD recorded approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges in Cost of sales during the three months ended June 28, 2025, associated with the U.S. government export control on its AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products [0000002488-25-000108:0012]. AMD's gross margin for that quarter was 40%, compared with 49% a year earlier, and the decrease was primarily due to this charge [0000002488-25-000108:0030]. AMD reported an operating loss of $134 million for the quarter, against operating income of $269 million a year earlier, and attributed the decline to lower gross margin and higher operating expenses [0000002488-25-000108:0030].

questions.question: What agreements with OpenAI do AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K and NVIDIA's fiscal 2026 10-K disclose, and how far had each progressed?

answer.text:
AMD entered into a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC in October 2025 to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the first gigawatt of capacity powered by AMD Instinct MI450 series products [0000002488-26-000018:0005][0000002488-26-000018:0006]. Concurrent with that agreement, AMD issued OpenAI a warrant to purchase up to 160 million shares of AMD common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share [0000002488-26-000018:0072][0000002488-26-000018:0117]. The warrant shares vest in tranches based on AMD Instinct GPU purchase milestones and achievement of specified AMD stock price targets and stock performance, and each vested tranche is also subject to other technical and commercial conditions before exercise [0000002488-26-000018:0072][0000002488-26-000018:0117]. The warrant is exercisable through October 5, 2030 [0000002488-26-000018:0117].
As of December 27, 2025, none of the warrant shares had met the vesting or exercise conditions, and the warrant had no impact on AMD's financial statements for the year [0000002488-26-000018:0072][0000002488-26-000018:0117]. AMD will account for the warrant shares as a liability until certain conditions for equity classification are satisfied [0000002488-26-000018:0117]. AMD's exhibit list also includes the warrant dated October 5, 2025 and a Registration Rights Agreement dated October 5, 2025 with OpenAI [0000002488-26-000018:0143][0000002488-26-000018:0148].
It says NVIDIA is finalizing an investment and partnership agreement with OpenAI, and that there is no assurance it will enter into such an agreement or that a transaction will be completed [0001045810-26-000021:0034][0001045810-26-000021:0071].

questions.question: After the U.S. government granted licenses in 2025 for some China-bound data center GPUs, what did NVIDIA (fiscal 2026 10-K) and AMD (fiscal 2025 10-K) report about licensed shipments and the U.S. government's expected revenue share?

answer.text:
On licensed shipments, AMD said that an April 2025 U.S. license requirement for certain semiconductor exports to China and D5 countries affects its AMD Instinct MI308 products, and that it incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. AMD said it applied for and was granted some licenses that allow it to ship MI308 products to certain China-based customers [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2025, AMD began shipping products and reversed approximately $360 million of those charges [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. AMD also said that sales of MI308 products into China depend on customer demand, China's import control rules and its ability to obtain licenses [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. For full-year 2025, AMD reported approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges tied to the MI308 export control [0000002488-26-000018:0070].
On the revenue share, AMD said that in August 2025 U.S. government officials expressed an expectation that the government will receive 15% of the revenue generated from licensed MI308 sales to China [0000002488-26-000018:0042]. AMD added that the government has not published a regulation establishing such a requirement [0000002488-26-000018:0043]. AMD said any request for a percentage of the revenue could subject it to litigation, increase its costs, harm its competitive position and benefit competitors that are not subject to such arrangements [0000002488-26-000018:0043].

questions.question: AMD's fiscal 2025 10-K names Altera as a competitor. What happened to Intel's ownership of Altera in 2025, and how does Intel now account for it?

answer.text:
The sale was agreed on April 14, 2025, when Altera was a wholly owned subsidiary [0000050863-26-000011:0031]. It closed on September 12, 2025, for net purchase consideration of $4.3 billion [0000050863-26-000011:0031].
Intel deconsolidated Altera from its Consolidated Financial Statements effective September 12, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0013]. Altera's results were included in Intel's "all other" category through September 11, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0013].
Intel retained a 49% minority interest, which it now accounts for as a non-marketable equity method investment [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. Intel concluded that Altera is a variable interest entity for which it is not the primary beneficiary, because the governance structure does not let Intel direct the activities that most significantly affect Altera's economic performance [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. The investment is classified within equity investments on the Consolidated Balance Sheets [0000050863-26-000011:0145].
As of December 27, 2025, the carrying value of the investment was $3.2 billion and Intel's ownership interest was 48% [0000050863-26-000011:0145]. The sale produced a pre-tax gain of $5.6 billion, recognized within interest and other, net [0000050863-26-000011:0146]. About $2.1 billion of that gain came from remeasuring the retained investment to fair value at the closing date [0000050863-26-000011:0147].

questions.question: What did AMD say drove its Data Center segment revenue growth in the second quarter of 2024, and how did the drivers and segment profitability differ in the second quarter of 2025?

answer.text:
In the second quarter of fiscal 2024, AMD's Data Center net revenue was $2.8 billion, up 115% from $1.3 billion in the prior year period, and AMD said the increase was primarily driven by the steep ramp of AMD Instinct GPU shipments and strong growth in 4th Gen AMD EPYC CPU sales [0000002488-24-000123:0026]. Data Center operating income for that quarter was $743 million, compared with $147 million a year earlier, and AMD attributed the increase primarily to higher revenue [0000002488-24-000123:0026].
In the second quarter of fiscal 2025, Data Center net revenue was $3.2 billion, up 14% from $2.8 billion, and the growth was primarily driven by growth in AMD EPYC CPU sales, with no mention of Instinct GPU shipments as a driver [0000002488-25-000108:0033]. Profitability reversed: Data Center had an operating loss of $155 million, compared with operating income of $743 million in the prior year period [0000002488-25-000108:0033]. AMD attributed the decrease primarily to approximately $800 million of inventory and related charges tied to the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 GPU products, along with higher R&D expense [0000002488-25-000108:0033].

cypher_attempts.query:
MATCH (:Company {ticker: 'INTC'})-[:FILED]->(f:Filing {form_type: '10-Q'})
WHERE f.fiscal_period IN ['FY2025-Q1', 'FY2024-Q1']
MATCH (f)-[r:REPORTS]->(m:MetricValue)-[:MEASURES]->(s)
WHERE (s:Segment OR s:MarketPlatform OR s:Product OR s:Company)
 AND (any(x IN [s.name] + coalesce(s.aliases, []) WHERE toLower(x) CONTAINS 'client' OR toLower(x) CONTAINS 'ccg' OR toLower(x) CONTAINS 'notebook' OR toLower(x) CONTAINS 'desktop')
 OR toLower(m.concept) CONTAINS 'client' OR toLower(m.concept) CONTAINS 'notebook' OR toLower(m.concept) CONTAINS 'desktop' OR toLower(m.concept) CONTAINS 'asp' OR toLower(m.concept) CONTAINS 'volume')
OPTIONAL MATCH (m)-[:EVIDENCED_BY]->(c:Chunk)-[:PART_OF]->(f)
WITH f, s, m, [cid IN r.chunk_ids WHERE cid STARTS WITH f.accession_no + ':'] AS edge_ids, collect(c.chunk_id) AS node_ids
WITH f, s, m, edge_ids + node_ids AS ids
WHERE size(ids) > 0
RETURN f.fiscal_period AS fiscal_period, s.name AS subject, m.concept AS concept, m.value AS value, m.unit AS unit, m.period AS period, ids AS chunk_ids
ORDER BY CASE WHEN toLower(m.concept) CONTAINS 'client' OR toLower(s.name) CONTAINS 'client' OR toLower(s.name) CONTAINS 'ccg' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END, f.fiscal_period DESC, size(ids) DESC
